findings.text: non-blocking: _stamp_terminal_launch_failure swallows CrewError from runs._mutate_pointer, so when the pointer write fails the request is left launch-failed carrying no failure text and the caller sees no signal, which is the state the limit branch exists to make visible.

non-blocking: the limit branch continues without appending a verdict row, so the admission result reports the request as neither requeued nor refused and a coordinator reading `requeued` and `verdicts` cannot see why a queued request stopped.

non-blocking: a request naming no repository falls back to Path.cwd(), the admit service's own directory, which reproduces the defect the node fixes for exactly the class of request that carries no repo; the docstring acknowledges the fallback but no test covers it.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from 3ab436fe38858d361bdd38ee97ab437d867b2043 to 97674dad7c12a717205f955148f6a0c4cc0ce0df; one implementation commit touching six modules and one test, one docs commit appending the landing fragment, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for three behaviours: a relative brief launches from an unrelated directory, an absent brief is refused before storage, and a request past its launch limit stays launch-failed with the failure text; tests/test_a_relative_brief_launches_from_any_directory.py:88, :114 and :172 assert each. The absent-brief refusal is pre-existing (reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2572 readable_brief_source feeds _brief_digest), verified not reimplemented.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a request stores its brief so every launcher resolves the same file; reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:829 resolves a relative brief against the request's repository once at dispatch, and the admit launcher passes that the launcher reads through reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:369.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261120T204920841876-qwnw-a-relative-brief-launches-from-any-directory/manifest.md; it records the scoped gate and both suite arms green and states the base arm 3 failed, 2 passed as the negative control beside five named logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: every one of the nine paths in the diff is inside the declared set; reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py were declared but left untouched.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_relative_brief_launches_from_any_directory.py:149 asserts the re-queued id is absent from result["requeued"], which reddens if reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:923's limit branch is deleted, as the recorded base arm shows for three of five cases.
justifications.evidence: the scoped gate at 47644df5 ran tests/test_a_relative_brief_launches_from_any_directory.py and reports 63 passed, the after arm 63 passed against a base arm of 58 passed, and the negative control at 3ab436fe reports 3 failed, 2 passed with EXIT=1.
justifications.fit: reckon/flight.py:1324 reads the new limit through the same queue namespace and fallbacks as reckon/flight.py:1300's queue_max_requests, and no added name carries a plan, version or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:829 makes node.brief absolute against the request's repository, so reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:369's dispatch reads one file from any working directory, and the endpoint's launch-failure clause is at reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:923.
justifications.reuse: reckon/flight.py:1324 extends the existing queue accessor family and reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:554 adds a capability no other module owns; a search of reckon/crew for repo-relative resolution found only reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1615, which matches cited paths to roots rather than resolving a dispatch argument.
justifications.scope_discipline: all nine changed paths sit inside the twelve declared, and the only untested-in-gate module touching the change, tests/test_a_queued_run_is_admitted.py:66, exercises only a first re-queue.
